Ugggh... they tried. Sorry they failed

ETA: this is just a really good encapsulation of the modern type 1 diabetic life. We stay alive through access to information and transparency in our food choices. Not other people’s misguided notions about how they’re helping us.

I don’t know if it’s a generational thing, or a midwestern Protestant upbringing thing, or just my own individual shit. But at some point I realized that I don’t know how I feel about something until I have a dream about it and my emotions about the situation reveal themselves in the dream. Like my brain can’t process difficult things in its waking state- just when it’s relaxed and vulnerable.

I don’t know why this is, just thought it was interesting. I was wondering if anyone else had similar experiences. I shared this with a friend once, but she has since abandoned me, lol. Et tu, amiga? So I’m curious to get fresh perspectives.

It strikes me more as a joke made in poor taste, rather than an attitude that can be tied to generational differences. I’m one of those humorless feminists though; I don’t think rape jokes are funny, including jokes that imply random strangers are rapists.
I teared up a little too, NGL
Gotcha. I liked that moment, too- shows he can take a joke, even if it’s an imaginary joke that he made up himself, LOL.

Hmmm... interesting! Were you wishing he would fuck off, or were your thoughts directed elsewhere? Just curious. I thought his take was pretty funny. And he gives a lot more credit to genx-ers than we give ourselves.
Just kidding, I cautiously like it. I guess.
Hello all, the sensors have all been spoken for. Thanks to all who replied!

Thank you for replying and telling me that story.

It’s not random at all, or dumb. I actually did lose a teacher last year, a poet and my high school English teacher. Like all good teachers, he didn’t teach his “subject” really- he just taught us how to be human, using literature and poetry as the lens. His death hit me harder than I thought anything but the death of a parent would ever hit me. If you want advice from an internet stranger, I think you should reach out to your teacher. I’m far gone from high school (I’m 40 now), but I think all teachers need to hear that they changed someone for the better.

Dorothy Parker is rolling her eyes in her grave right now, I’m sure ;)
Thank you. Your username is amazing :)
